draft.title: Japan's expansion
card: After the Meiji Restoration, Japan built a strong army and navy. It wanted to be treated as an equal by the Western powers and to gain land and resources.
Japan defeated China in a war in 1894 to 1895. It then defeated Russia in a war in 1904 to 1905, which showed that an Asian power could beat a European one.
Japan took control of Korea and made it part of its empire in 1910. In 1931 its army invaded Manchuria, a region of north-east China, and Japan set up a state there that it controlled.
Japan kept pushing into China and Southeast Asia. This growing empire led Japan into World War II.
draft.remember: Japan used its new military strength to win wars and take land, building an empire that led to World War II.

a.q: Why did Japan's defeat of Russia in 1904 to 1905 matter?
opts: It showed an Asian power could beat a European one
It gave Japan control of Korea as a gift from Russia
It ended Japan's empire and its plans to expand
It forced Japan to open its ports to foreign trade
a.why: Japan's modern army and navy beat a European power, which showed how strong Japan had become. Korea was taken later, in 1910, and Japan's empire grew after this war rather than ending.
a.clue: Think about what a win over a European power showed.

b.q: In 1931 Japan's army invaded Manchuria and set up a state it controlled there. Which statement best describes what this shows about Japan?
opts: It was using force to build an empire on the Asian mainland
It was giving up its army to focus on trade and peace
It was defending Korea from an attack by Russia
It was opening its ports to foreign ships for the first time
b.why: The invasion of Manchuria, part of China, was an act of expansion by force. It was one step in the empire that led into World War II. Japan did not give up its army, and Korea had already been taken in 1910.
b.clue: Manchuria was a region of north-east China, and Japan's army controlled it afterwards.

a.best: It showed an Asian power could beat a European one

b.best: It was using force to build an empire on the Asian mainland

a.q: Why did Japan's defeat of Russia in 1904 to 1905 matter?
opts: It showed an Asian power could beat a European one
It showed Western armies were still too strong for Asia
It ended Japan's plans to gain land and resources
It made Japan give up its army and navy
a.why: Russia was a European power, so Japan's win showed that an Asian power could beat one. It did not show Western armies were too strong, since Japan won, and Japan's empire kept growing after this war rather than ending.
a.clue: Ask which side won, and where each side came from.

b.q: In 1931 Japan's army invaded Manchuria and set up a state it controlled there. Which statement best describes what this shows about Japan?
opts: It was using force to build an empire on the Asian mainland
It was giving up its army to focus on trade and peace
It was defending Korea from an attack by Russia
It was opening its ports to foreign ships for the first time
b.why: The invasion of Manchuria, part of China, was an act of expansion by force. It was one step in the empire that led into World War II. Japan did not give up its army, and Korea had already been part of Japan's empire since 1910.
b.clue: Ask whether Manchuria belonged to Japan before 1931.
